title: First assignment: a bounded framing audit
hypothesis: Does density address the binding constraint better than feasible alternatives in one specified service?
physical_mechanism: More usable stored energy for a fixed system mass or volume can matter only where that constraint limits the service.
required_assumptions: The case, service quality, comparators and constraints are fixed before evaluation.
Evidence is licensed, traceable and comparable.
cheapest_discriminating_experiment: Select one useful service with a relevant practitioner; record beneficiary and unmet need.
Register functional unit, boundary, geography, lifetime, baseline, alternatives, minimum improvement and hard constraints before reviewing comparative outcomes.
Collect source-level evidence and prior art; record missing data and failed approaches.
Compare feasible interventions at matched service quality and reliability; propagate uncertainty and test sensitivity.
Ask an independent reviewer to reproduce calculations and challenge excluded boundaries.
Publish evidence and a retain, narrow, replace or unresolved decision; revise the next question.
required_equipment: access to source literature and datasets
expected_uncertainty: Not yet quantified; register measurement ranges, source quality, dependence and model sensitivity before comparison.
safety_considerations: Desk analysis only. This protocol authorizes no physical experiment.
falsification_result: A feasible alternative robustly dominates density, density does not address the binding constraint, or it fails a preregistered threshold or safety/environmental constraint.
replication_procedure: Freeze source snapshots or checksums, licensed data, code, units and assumptions; a separate reviewer reproduces the comparison and records disagreement and source overlap.

preregistration.missing_reason: Protocol is proposed, not ready to execute or an experimental result.
